companies.name: Spruce Pine high-purity quartz (The Quartz Corp & Sibelco)
companies.role: Mines and refines the ultra-pure quartz sand used to make the crucibles that hold molten silicon
companies.description: Almost every silicon wafer on Earth begins in one Appalachian valley: Spruce Pine, North Carolina, where two companies - Belgian miner Sibelco (IOTA brand) and Norwegian-French joint venture The Quartz Corp - dig quartz pure enough to be melted into the crucibles that hold molten silicon during crystal pulling. Estimates put 70-90% of the world's semiconductor- and solar-grade high-purity quartz supply at roughly 20,000 tonnes a year from these two mines, refined to 99.999% SiO2 (partly at The Quartz Corp's plant in Drag, Norway). A crucible made from lesser quartz sheds contaminants straight into the melt and ruins the ingot, which is why no substitute deposit has been qualified at scale. Hurricane Helene shut both mines in September 2024 and briefly focused the entire chip industry on a town of 2,000 people.

companies.name: TOTO Ltd.
companies.role: Ultra-pure alumina electrostatic chucks that hold silicon wafers inside etch and litho tools
companies.description: TOTO is the Kitakyushu company that makes the world's most famous toilets - and, since 1988, the ceramic electrostatic chucks (ESCs) that clamp a wafer in place with electrostatic force instead of mechanical clamps, which would warp it, or adhesive, which cannot be removed cleanly. The chucks are pressed from ultra-pure aluminium oxide with a secret additive blend, barely expand when heated, and carry machined channels for coolant so the wafer survives a plasma etch chamber; a dinner-plate-sized part can cost six figures. TOTO is one of only two suppliers at the leading edge of this market and is a key source for Lam Research's cryogenic 3D NAND etchers. By FY2025 its advanced-ceramics division was throwing off roughly 40% operating margins and had overtaken the housing business as the group's biggest profit source - data-centre customers are now outbidding hotels for TOTO's best ceramicists.

companies.name: Ajinomoto Co., Inc.
companies.role: Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF), the insulating film inside almost every advanced chip package substrate
companies.description: The company that introduced the world to MSG also holds a near-total monopoly on the insulating film beneath modern CPUs and GPUs. Launched in 1999 out of Ajinomoto's amino-acid and fine-chemistry expertise, ABF is an epoxy/hardener/silica composite that is a stable dielectric, can be patterned at very fine pitch, and takes copper plating unusually well - a combination nobody has credibly matched. Ajinomoto holds well over 95% of the interlayer-insulation market for high-end package substrates, and layer counts have climbed from four or five to well past a dozen on an AI accelerator. It is investing about Y25bn to lift ABF capacity roughly 50% by 2030 across its Kawasaki and Gunma sites, where margins on the film now exceed 50%.

companies.name: IBIDEN Co., Ltd.
companies.role: FC-BGA package substrates - the green board an AI die is soldered onto
companies.description: Ibiden, a former hydroelectric utility in Ogaki, Gifu, is one of only two companies that can build the highest-end flip-chip package substrates at volume. It laminates Ajinomoto's ABF film with copper, drills tens of thousands of microscopic vias, and turns it into the multi-layer square that a CPU or GPU die is mounted on. Its customers include Nvidia, Intel, AMD, TSMC and Samsung, and demand has been so far ahead of supply that customers buy everything it makes. In February 2026 Ibiden announced roughly $3.2bn of investment across FY2026-28 on top of the Ono and Kawama plant build-outs, aiming to multiply AI-substrate capacity.

suppliesTo.what: FC-BGA package substrates for AI accelerators

companies.name: Unimicron Technology Corp.
companies.role: ABF/FC-BGA package substrates and high-layer-count PCBs for AI accelerators
companies.description: Unimicron, headquartered in Guishan, Taoyuan, is the other half of the ABF substrate duopoly alongside Ibiden and the largest IC-substrate maker by revenue. It takes Ajinomoto's build-up film, sandwiches it with copper and drills the microvia stacks that turn it into the substrate a GPU die sits on. Analysts put Unimicron at roughly 35% of ABF substrate supply for Nvidia's high-end GPUs and above 50% for custom AI ASICs such as Google TPU and AWS Trainium. Its Guangfu plant in Hukou, Hsinchu went to mass production ahead of schedule in late 2024 specifically for high-end AI parts, and it also builds substrates feeding TSMC's CoWoS packaging line.

companies.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical Co., Ltd.
companies.role: The world's largest maker of bare 300mm silicon wafers (via Shin-Etsu Handotai)
companies.description: Shin-Etsu is the world's number one silicon wafer supplier, holding roughly 30% of the market on its own; together with SUMCO the two Japanese firms account for about half of all wafers made. Its Shin-Etsu Handotai arm melts electronic-grade polysilicon in quartz crucibles, pulls it into single-crystal ingots by the Czochralski process, then slices, laps and polishes them into the mirror-finish discs every chip starts life on. Shin-Etsu also makes photoresists and other fab chemicals. The fragility of this step is not theoretical: a 2021 fire at one of Shin-Etsu's suppliers helped trigger the global chip shortage that left half-finished cars sitting on dealer lots for two years.
companies.imageCredit: Kakidai / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) - Marunouchi Eiraku Building, Shin-Etsu head office

companies.name: SUMCO Corporation
companies.role: Number two global supplier of 300mm silicon wafers
companies.description: SUMCO, formed from the silicon businesses of Sumitomo Metal Industries and Mitsubishi Materials, is the world's second-largest silicon wafer maker with roughly a quarter to a third of the market. It grows single crystals at Saga, Yonezawa and other sites, centralises wafering at Imari in Kyushu, and opened a dedicated 300mm epitaxial wafer plant in Chitose, Hokkaido - conveniently close to Rapidus. Between SUMCO and Shin-Etsu, two Japanese companies supply about half the bare silicon that every fab on the planet consumes.
companies.imageCredit: Yamaguchi Yoshiaki / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0) - SEAVANS, Minato-ku, SUMCO head office

companies.name: GlobalWafers Co., Ltd.
companies.role: Taiwan's silicon wafer maker, roughly the world's third largest
companies.description: GlobalWafers, spun out of Sino-American Silicon and headquartered in Hsinchu, is the largest non-Japanese wafer supplier with about 17% of the silicon wafer market and 18 plants across nine countries. Its 2016 purchase of SunEdison Semiconductor (the old MEMC) gave it a US footprint, and in 2025 it opened a $3.5bn 300mm fab in Sherman, Texas - the first new advanced silicon wafer plant built in the United States in more than twenty years - with a further $4bn of US expansion announced. That matters because until Sherman, essentially no leading-edge 300mm wafers were made on American soil.
companies.imageCredit: Sebastian Wallroth / Wikimedia Commons (public domain) - single-crystal silicon boule

companies.name: Siltronic AG
companies.description: Siltronic, spun out of Wacker Chemie and headquartered in Munich, is the only significant Western European maker of hyperpure silicon wafers and roughly the world's fourth largest. Its story starts with the first high-purity silicon crystal pulled at Burghausen in 1953; today it pulls crystals and polishes wafers up to 300mm at Burghausen and Freiberg in Germany, Portland in the US, and Singapore. Its largest capacity is in Singapore, where the new FabNext plant in the Tampines Wafer Fab Park was inaugurated in 2024 and brought epitaxial wafer capability to the island for the first time. Together with Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers and SK Siltron, the top five suppliers control over 80% of global 300mm capacity.
companies.imageCredit: Hebbe / Wikimedia Commons (public domain) - bare silicon wafers

companies.name: JSR Corporation
companies.role: The world's largest photoresist maker, including EUV and metal-oxide resists
companies.description: JSR - once Japan Synthetic Rubber, a 1957 state-founded synthetic rubber company - is now the world's biggest photoresist supplier with roughly 27% of the market. Photoresist is the light-sensitive polymer that actually records the pattern an ASML scanner projects; nothing gets printed without it. JSR's 2021 acquisition of Oregon-based Inpria gave it the leading metal-oxide EUV resist, a chemistry many believe is required for High-NA EUV, and it runs its EUV resist development next to imec in Leuven, Belgium. In 2024 the Japanese state-backed fund JIC took JSR private in a $6.4bn deal explicitly aimed at keeping this material under Japanese control; JSR is now building its first Taiwanese photoresist plant to sit next to TSMC.

companies.name: Tokyo Ohka Kogyo Co., Ltd. (TOK)
companies.role: Photoresists and lithography chemicals, from legacy nodes to EUV
companies.description: Founded in 1940 and based in Kawasaki, TOK is one of a handful of Japanese chemical houses that between them supply the overwhelming majority of the world's photoresist. It covers the full range - i-line and KrF for legacy automotive and analogue chips, ArF immersion, and EUV resists for leading-edge logic and DRAM - alongside developers, strippers and other wet chemistry. Its Sagami Operation Center in Samukawa, Kanagawa is the R&D hub and main resist plant. TOK is not a strict monopoly (JSR, Shin-Etsu, Sumitomo and Fujifilm compete), but the concentration of photoresist supply in a few Japanese sites is itself one of the industry's quieter single points of failure.

companies.name: Air Liquide S.A.
companies.role: Ultra-high-purity bulk and specialty gases piped straight into fabs
companies.description: A fab is, among other things, an enormous gas consumer: nitrogen to purge every chamber, hydrogen and helium for EUV and cooling, and dozens of exotic specialty gases and precursors for deposition, etch and doping. Air Liquide, founded in Paris in 1902, is one of two companies that can build, own and operate the on-site air separation and specialty gas plants that a leading-edge fab needs, and it runs its electronics division out of Tokyo to sit close to Asian customers. It signed long-term supply agreements for TSMC's Arizona site and for the semiconductor cluster around Dresden. Purity is measured in parts per billion; a contaminated gas line can scrap an entire lot.

companies.name: Linde plc
companies.role: Industrial and electronic specialty gases, on-site air separation units for fabs
companies.description: Linde - the 2018 merger of Germany's Linde AG and America's Praxair, now with executive offices in Woking, UK - is the other half of the electronics gas duopoly with Air Liquide. It builds, owns and operates air separation units next to fabs to deliver ultra-high-purity nitrogen, oxygen, argon and hydrogen by pipeline, plus the specialty gas mixtures used in deposition, etch, doping and chamber cleaning. In 2026 it committed roughly $1bn to expand its Phoenix on-site complex with two more SPECTRA air separation units on top of the three already there, its largest electronics investment anywhere, and about $800m more through its Taiwanese joint venture Linde LienHwa.

companies.name: HOYA Corporation
companies.role: EUV and optical mask blanks - the defect-free substrates every chip pattern is written onto
companies.description: Before a pattern can be printed onto a wafer it has to exist on a photomask, and that mask starts as a blank: an ultra-flat low-thermal-expansion glass substrate coated with a 40-plus-layer molybdenum/silicon multilayer that reflects EUV light. Hoya, better known for eyeglass lenses and endoscopes, is one of only two companies on Earth (with AGC) that can make EUV mask blanks at production quality - estimates of Hoya's EUV share range from about a third to over 75% depending on the survey, but the duopoly itself is undisputed. A single killer defect in that multilayer stack ruins a mask that can cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. Hoya makes its EUV blanks in Japan and announced roughly $400m to expand capacity, with a high-volume EUV blank line planned for Singapore.

companies.name: TANAKA Precious Metals (Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo)
companies.role: Gold, copper and silver bonding wire that connects a die to its package
companies.description: Tanaka has been refining precious metals in Tokyo since 1885 and drew its first ultra-fine gold bonding wire in 1964. Bonding wire is the hair-thin conductor that stitches a chip die to its package leads - critical for the stacked memory dies inside DRAM and HBM modules, where wires only a few microns across have to be looped tens of thousands of times without a single break. Tanaka is the largest single supplier, with roughly a quarter to a third of the market by length, and together with Germany's Heraeus accounts for over 40% of world supply. Bonding wire is made by its TANAKA Denshi Kogyo arm in Yoshinogari, Saga, with plants in Singapore, Malaysia, China and Taiwan.
